title: A Scalable Multi Task Learning Framework for Modeling Demographic Disagreements in Annotation Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2611.21458v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Annotators from different demographic backgrounds often disagree in systematic ways due to varying lived experiences, cultural contexts, and their relationship to the content. When such disagreement occurs, one group's perspective may sometimes warrant prioritization because they hold an epistemically advantaged standpoint or bear greater stake in the outcome. For example, when assessing toxicity of posts on social media, it may be important to prioritize a targeted group's viewpoint. We propose a Stakeholder-Aware Joint Multi-Task Learning (SAJ-MTL) framework to jointly model demographic disagreement both across- and within- annotator groups. The model uses conditional gradient routing to handle sparsity induced by group-conditional labeling, and parameterization supports customized weighting of groups in different task settings. translated_title: 一种用于建模标注任务中人口统计群体分歧的可扩展多任务学习框架
translated_abstract: 来自不同人口统计背景的标注者由于不同的生活经历、文化背景以及与内容的关系，往往会以系统性的方式产生分歧。当这种分歧发生时，某一群体的观点有时值得被优先考虑，因为他们可能拥有认知上的优势立场，或对结果有更大的利害关系。例如，在评估社交媒体帖子的毒性时，优先考虑被针对群体的观点可能非常重要。我们提出了一个利益相关者感知的联合多任务学习（SAJ-MTL）框架，以联合建模标注者群体之间以及群体内部的人口统计分歧。该模型使用条件梯度路由来处理由群体条件标注引起的稀疏性问题，并且其参数化设计支持在不同任务设置中对不同群体进行自定义加权。SAJ-MTL 通过对上下文的更好理解，提升了毒性检测任务中的群体级性能。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种利益相关者感知的联合多任务学习框架（SAJ-MTL），通过条件梯度路由和可自定义的群体加权机制，联合建模标注者群体间及群体内的人口统计分歧，从而显著提升毒性检测等任务中的群体级性能。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a Stakeholder-Aware Joint Multi-Task Learning (SAJ-MTL) framework that uses conditional gradient routing and customizable group weighting to jointly model demographic disagreements both across and within annotator groups, improving group-level performance in toxicity detection tasks.
